visuals.title: Where the mass effects hit
visuals.text: The pituitary sits under the brain with the optic chiasm just above it, so headache and visual field loss are the mass effects.

glossary.mass effect: Symptoms caused by a growth pressing on nearby structures rather than by hormones.
glossary.hormonal excess: Too much of a hormone being produced, here by a secreting tumour.
glossary.functional tumour: A tumour that produces a hormone.
glossary.coagulopathy: A problem with blood clotting that raises the risk of bleeding.
glossary.ED: Erectile dysfunction: difficulty getting or keeping an erection.
glossary.infertility: Difficulty conceiving after a year of regular unprotected sex.
glossary.normocytic anaemia: Low haemoglobin with red cells of normal size.
glossary.hypothyroidism: Underactive thyroid with too little thyroid hormone.
glossary.colorectal cancer: Cancer of the colon or rectum.
glossary.risperidone: An atypical antipsychotic that blocks dopamine and so can raise prolactin.
glossary.haloperidol: A typical antipsychotic that blocks dopamine receptors, raising prolactin.
glossary.tricyclics: Older antidepressants, such as amitriptyline, that can raise prolactin.
glossary.SSRIs: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, common antidepressants such as sertraline.
glossary.parathyroid hyperplasia: Enlargement of all the parathyroid glands, causing excess parathyroid hormone.
glossary.parathyroid adenoma: Benign tumour of one parathyroid gland making excess parathyroid hormone.
glossary.peptic ulceration: Ulcers in the stomach or duodenum, here from excess gastrin.
glossary.cardiomyopathy: Disease of the heart muscle that weakens or stiffens it.
glossary.diabetes insipidus: Passing large volumes of dilute urine because ADH is lacking or the kidneys ignore it.
glossary.MEN type 1: Inherited syndrome of parathyroid, pituitary and pancreatic tumours.
glossary.MRI pituitary: Magnetic resonance scan focused on the pituitary gland, the best imaging for adenomas.
glossary.pituitary function tests: Blood tests of all pituitary hormones and their target hormones.
glossary.ACTH: Adrenocorticotropic hormone: pituitary hormone that drives cortisol release from the adrenal glands.
glossary.cortisol: Steroid stress hormone from the adrenal cortex, vital for blood pressure and glucose.
glossary.TSH: Thyroid stimulating hormone, made by the pituitary to drive the thyroid.
glossary.T4: Thyroxine, the main hormone released by the thyroid gland.
glossary.thyroxine: Thyroid hormone (T4), given as levothyroxine for replacement.
glossary.sex hormones: Oestrogen, progesterone or testosterone, replaced when gonadotrophins fail.
glossary.growth hormone: Pituitary hormone that drives growth and metabolism, mostly through IGF-1.
glossary.monoclonal: Grown from one single abnormal cell.
glossary.anterior pituitary: Front lobe of the pituitary, making prolactin, GH, ACTH, TSH, LH and FSH.
glossary.pituitary fossa: Bony hollow in the sphenoid bone that holds the pituitary gland; also called the sella turcica.
glossary.suprasellar extension: Growth of a pituitary tumour upward out of the sella towards the optic chiasm.
glossary.nasal retinal fibres: Nerve fibres from the inner half of each retina that cross at the chiasm and carry the temporal fields.
glossary.insulin resistance: Reduced response of cells to insulin, raising blood glucose.
glossary.infarction: Tissue death from loss of blood supply.
glossary.acute adrenal insufficiency: Sudden lack of cortisol causing shock, low sodium and collapse; an adrenal crisis.
glossary.radiotherapy: Treatment using targeted radiation to destroy tumour cells.
glossary.surgical decompression: An operation to relieve pressure, here on the optic chiasm.
glossary.neurosurgical review: Urgent assessment by the brain surgery team.
glossary.seizures: Episodes of abnormal electrical brain activity causing fits or altered awareness.
glossary.hypercalcaemia: Raised calcium in the blood, here from parathyroid disease in MEN 1.
glossary.functional status: Whether a tumour is producing hormone or not.
